title: Inductive step: Hilbert series of ker(pi-bar) (kernel identity)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Inductive step / kernel Hilbert series.**

In the reduction of the main identity $(\star)$ to a recursion in $k$, the comparison surjection $\pi:R^{k,\ell}\twoheadrightarrow R^{k-1,\ell}$ (with $\pi(e_i)=e_i$ for $i\le k-1$, $\pi(e_k)=0$, kernel $e_kR^{k,\ell}$) respects the filtration and yields
$$Q_{k,\ell,m}(q)-Q_{k-1,\ell,m}(q)=\mathrm{Hilb}(\ker\overline\pi;q),$$
where $\overline\pi:R^{k,\ell,m}/R^{k,\ell,m-1}\twoheadrightarrow R^{k-1,\ell,m}/R^{k-1,\ell,m-1}$ and
$$\ker\overline\pi\cong\{x\in R^{k,\ell,m}:\pi(x)\in R^{k-1,\ell,m-1}\}/R^{k,\ell,m-1}.$$

**To prove (currently only checked symbolically for $1\le k,\ell\le5$):** for $1\le m\le\ell$, $m<k$,
$$\mathrm{Hilb}(\ker\overline\pi;q)=q^{\,m+(k-m)(\ell-m+1)}\binom{\ell}{m}_q\binom{k-1}{m-1}_q.\qquad(\dagger)$$

This is the entire mathematical content of the inductive step: it produces the exact generating function, not merely the shape of a recursion. The reduction to $(\dagger)$ is rigorous; the identity itself is unproved from first principles.

**Why it is hard.**
- $\mathbb Q\langle e_1,\dots,e_m\rangle\subseteq R^{k,\ell}$ is not a sub-Hopf-algebra; its Schur expansion is opaque, so the graded dimensions cannot be read off the Pieri rule directly.
- The product $\binom{\ell}{m}_q\binom{k-1}{m-1}_q$ strongly suggests the kernel is modeled by **pairs** $(\nu,\rho)$ with $\nu\subseteq m\times(\ell-m)$ and $\rho\subseteq(m-1)\times(k-m)$. The crux is to construct an explicit basis / filtration realizing this product **with the exact degree shift** $m+(k-m)(\ell-m+1)$.

**Suggested attack.** Build a leading-term (Gröbner-style) basis of $R^{k,\ell,m}/R^{k,\ell,m-1}$ compatible with $\pi$, ordering monomials $e_1^{a_1}\cdots e_m^{a_m}$ and computing their leading Schur terms under the truncated vertical-strip Pieri rule. Show the new length-$k$ classes (those in $\ker\pi=e_kR^{k,\ell}=\mathrm{span}\{\overline{s_\lambda}:\ell(\lambda)=k\}$) reachable inside the $e_1,\dots,e_m$ subalgebra are indexed exactly by such pairs $(\nu,\rho)$, with degree $m+(k-m)(\ell-m+1)+|\nu|+|\rho|$. Use $\binom{k-1}{m-1}_q=\binom{k-1}{k-m}_q$ for a possible complementation bijection.

**Status.** Critic re-verified $(\star)$ (hence $(\dagger)$ as its inductive increment) for all $1\le k,\ell\le4$, $1\le m\le\ell$, via truncated-Pieri row reduction: the target is correct; only a general-$k$ proof is missing.
